lessons.title: Virgüllü ilgi cümleleri
lessons.goal: Defining ve non-defining ilgi cümlelerini ayırt edebilir ve virgülle ek bilgi verebilirim.

discover.title: Mardin'e bir hafta sonu
discover.body:
Mardin, which sits on a hill above the Mesopotamian plain, is one of the most beautiful cities in Turkey.

The old town, where honey-coloured stone houses climb up the hillside, looks like something from another century. Our guide, Şeyma, who has lived here all her life, took us through narrow streets full of small workshops.

The hotel that we stayed in was a 200-year-old mansion. From our room, which had a tiny balcony, we could see the plain stretching all the way to Syria.

In the evening, we tried a local dish called kaburga dolması, which was absolutely delicious.

options: On a hill above a plain
questions.explanation: "which sits on a hill above the Mesopotamian plain"
"Our guide, Şeyma, who has lived here all her life"

learn.explanation:
B1'de **defining** (tanımlayıcı) ilgi cümlelerini öğrendiniz. **Non-defining** (tanımlayıcı olmayan) ilgi cümleleri, zaten belli olan bir kişi ya da şey hakkında **ek bilgi** verir.

| Defining | Non-defining |
|---|---|
| **Hangisi** olduğunu söyler | **Ek bilgi** verir; çıkarılsa da anlam bozulmaz |
| **Virgül yok** | **Virgül var** (yazıda), konuşmada duraklama |
| who, which, **that** | who, which (**that olmaz**) |
| Zamir atlanabilir (nesne ise) | Zamir **asla atlanmaz** |
| The hotel **that we stayed in** was old. | Our hotel, **which was 200 years old**, ... |

**Karşılaştırın:**

- My brother **who lives in Paris** is a chef. (Birden fazla erkek kardeşim var; Paris'teki aşçı.)
- My brother, **who lives in Paris**, is a chef. (Tek erkek kardeşim var; ek bilgi: Paris'te yaşıyor.)

**Özel isimler** (Mardin, Şeyma, my mother) zaten belirli olduğu için genellikle **non-defining** alır:

- **Mardin, which** sits on a hill, ...
- **Şeyma, who** has lived here all her life, ...

**whose** ve **where** de non-defining olarak kullanılabilir: The old town, **where** ..., / Ali, **whose** father ..., ...

examples.en: Istanbul, which is divided by the Bosphorus, is on two continents.
examples.tr: Boğaz'la ikiye ayrılan İstanbul iki kıtada yer alır.

examples.en: My grandmother, who is 90, still swims every day.

examples.tr: Efes'i ziyaret ettik, orada Celsus Kütüphanesi'ni gördük.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "90 yaşındaki büyükannem" gibi ek bilgiler ismin önüne gelir ve virgül kullanılmaz. İngilizcede bu tür ek bilgiler non-defining relative clause ile ismin arkasına, virgüller arasında verilir. En sık hata, non-defining cümlelerde "that" kullanmaktır: "Mardin, that is in the south-east" yanlıştır; "Mardin, which is in the south-east" doğrudur.

options: Ankara, that is the capital, is in central Turkey.
Ankara, which is the capital, is in central Turkey.

My best friend, who I've known since primary school, is getting married next month. Konya, which is in central Anatolia, is famous for Mevlana. The Mevlana Museum, which attracts millions of visitors, is beautiful. Our old neighbourhood, where I grew up, has changed a lot.

lessons.title: Ki bu da...
lessons.goal: which ile bütün bir cümleye yorum ekleyebilir ve anlatımımı daha akıcı hale getirebilirim.

learn.explanation:
**which** bütün bir **cümleye** (sadece bir isme değil) **yorum** ekleyebilir. Önünde **her zaman virgül** olur.

| Cümle | Yorum (which = bu durum) |
|---|---|
| It didn't rain once, | **which** was lucky. |
| Our flight was delayed, | **which** meant we missed the first night. |
| They kept inviting us for dinner, | **which** made the trip special. |

Bu yapıda **which = and this / and that**:

- It didn't rain, **which** was lucky. = It didn't rain, **and this** was lucky.

**Dikkat:**

- Bu kullanımda **what** ya da **that** kullanılmaz: ~~It didn't rain, what was lucky.~~
- **which** ile başlayan yeni bir cümle yazıda kullanılmaz: ~~It didn't rain. Which was lucky.~~ (Konuşmada duyulabilir.)

**Sık kullanılan yorumlar:**

- ..., **which was a relief / a shame / a surprise**.
- ..., **which meant (that)** ...
- ..., **which is why** ...
- ..., **which made me** + sıfat / fiil

examples.en: The museum was closed, which was a real shame.
examples.tr: Müze kapalıydı, bu gerçekten yazık oldu.

examples.en: He spoke perfect Turkish, which surprised everyone.
examples.tr: Mükemmel Türkçe konuşuyordu, bu herkesi şaşırttı.

examples.en: The hotel was full, which is why we stayed in a guesthouse.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "... ki bu da ..." ya da "... bu da ... oldu" yapıları, İngilizcedeki cümleye yorum ekleyen which'e denk gelir. Türkçe konuşanlar bu durumda sık sık "what" kullanır: "It rained, what was terrible" yanlıştır; doğrusu "It rained, which was terrible".

options: It rained all week, what was terrible.
It rained all week, which was terrible.

task.prompt: Son seyahatinizi anlatın ve en az 5 olayı which ile yorumlayın: which was lucky / a shame / a relief / a surprise, which meant ..., which is why ..., which made me ...
task.modelAnswer: Last summer I went to Antalya with my family. We arrived at midnight, which meant we were all exhausted. The hotel gave us a bigger room, which was a nice surprise. It was 40 degrees every day, which is why we spent most of the time in the sea. My brother lost his phone on the beach, which was a disaster. But a stranger found it, which restored my faith in people!

lessons.title: Edatlı ve miktarlı ilgi cümleleri
lessons.goal: Edat + which / whom ve some of which / most of whom gibi yapılarla daha resmî ve ayrıntılı tanımlar yapabilirim.

discover.title: Rehber kitaptan: Van Gölü
discover.body:
Lake Van, which is the largest lake in Turkey, lies in the far east of the country at an altitude of about 1,650 metres.

The lake, the water of which is extremely salty and alkaline, has very few fish species. The best known is the inci kefali, which swims from the lake up into the rivers each spring to lay its eggs.

The region has many historical sites, most of which date back to the Urartian period. On Akdamar Island, to which boats run regularly in summer, you can visit a beautiful tenth-century Armenian church.

The local people, many of whom speak several languages, are known for their warm hospitality. Don't leave without trying a Van breakfast, for which the city is famous.

questions.prompt: What is special about Lake Van's water?
What is the city of Van famous for?
questions.explanation: "a Van breakfast, for which the city is famous"

learn.explanation:
**1. Edat + which / whom** (daha resmî)

Günlük dilde edat cümlenin **sonunda** kalır; resmî yazıda **which / whom'dan önce** gelir.

| Günlük | Resmî |
|---|---|
| The island **(which) boats run to** ... | The island, **to which** boats run, ... |
| The city **(that) it's famous for** ... | ... **for which** the city is famous |
| The man **(who) I spoke to** ... | The man **to whom** I spoke ... |

**Dikkat:** Edattan sonra **who** ve **that** kullanılmaz: ~~to who~~ / ~~to that~~ → **to whom** / **to which**

**2. Miktar + of which / of whom**

| Yapı | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **some of which** | There are many sites, **some of which** are 3,000 years old. |
| **most of whom** | The locals, **most of whom** speak Kurdish and Turkish, ... |
| **all of which** | We visited five museums, **all of which** were free. |
| **none of whom** | I met ten people, **none of whom** spoke English. |
| **both of which** | It has two beaches, **both of which** are unspoilt. |
| **the water of which** / **whose water** | The lake, **whose water** is salty, ... |

İnsanlar için **whom**, şeyler için **which** kullanılır.

examples.en: The village, to which there is only one road, is very peaceful.
examples.tr: Tek bir yolla ulaşılan köy çok huzurlu.

examples.en: We met many travellers, most of whom were from Europe.

learn.turkishNote: "... hepsi görülmeye değer", "... çoğu Avrupalıydı" gibi Türkçe yapılar İngilizcede "all of which", "most of whom" ile kurulur. Türkçe konuşanlar genellikle bunu iki ayrı cümle olarak söyler ("...three parks. All of them are..."). Bu da doğrudur, ama of which / of whom yapısı yazıda daha akıcı ve ileri bir seviye gösterir. "most of them" ile "most of whom" karıştırılmamalıdır: virgülden sonra tek cümlede "whom" gerekir.

task.modelAnswer: Kars, which is in north-eastern Turkey, is famous for its cheese and honey, for which people travel from all over the country. The city has many Russian-style buildings, most of which were built in the 19th century. Nearby is Ani, to which tourists come to see the ancient ruins. The region has several lakes, some of which freeze completely in winter. The locals, most of whom are farmers, are very welcoming.

lessons.title: Manzarayı anlatmak
lessons.goal: Coğrafya, manzara ve kültür kelimeleriyle bir yeri canlı ve özgün bir şekilde betimleyebilirim.

lines.speaker: Vlogger
lines.text: Good morning from Pamukkale! Behind me you can see the famous white terraces, which look like snow but are actually made of limestone.

learn.explanation:
**Bir yeri betimlerken kullanılan dil:**

| Konum | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **lie / be situated / be located** | The village **lies** in a green valley. |
| **overlook** | The castle **overlooks** the sea. |
| **stretch** | The beach **stretches** for 10 km. |
| **surround** | It's **surrounded by** mountains. |
| **be home to** | The park **is home to** rare birds. |

**Güçlü betimleme sıfatları:**

| Doğa | Şehir / kültür |
|---|---|
| breathtaking, stunning | bustling, lively, vibrant |
| unspoilt, remote | picturesque, charming |
| rugged (engebeli), lush (yemyeşil) | ancient, historic |

**"Klişe"den kaçının:** "beautiful" ve "nice" yerine daha özgün kelimeler seçin.

- ~~The beach was nice.~~ → The beach **stretched for miles**, and the sand was **as white as flour**.

**Duyuları kullanın:** Ne gördünüz, ne duydunuz, ne kokladınız, ne tattınız?

- The air **smelled of** jasmine. / You can **hear** the call to prayer echoing across the valley.

**Tavsiye dili:** **Don't miss** ... / **It's well worth** + -ing / **Avoid** ... / **The best time to visit is** ...

examples.en: The village lies at the foot of a rugged mountain.
examples.tr: Köy engebeli bir dağın eteğinde yer alıyor.

examples.en: The town is surrounded by lush green forests.
It's well worth getting up early to see the sunrise.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçe gezi yazılarında "muhteşem", "harika" gibi sıfatlar sık tekrarlanır. İngilizce gezi yazısında okuyucu somut ayrıntı ve özgün betimleme bekler: "It was amazing" yerine ne gördüğünüzü, duyduğunuzu ve hissettiğinizi anlatın. "customs" kelimesine de dikkat: tekil "custom" gelenek, çoğul "customs" çoğunlukla gümrük anlamındadır.

options: The village lies in a valley.
The village lays in a valley.

task.modelAnswer: Hi everyone, I'm in Uzungöl, which lies in a lush green valley in the mountains above Trabzon. The lake is surrounded by pine forests, and the air smells of wood and rain. Behind me, wooden houses climb up the rugged hillside. It's breathtaking in the early morning, when the mist covers the water. My tips: avoid weekends in August, when it's crowded, and don't miss the local trout!

lessons.title: Gezi yazısı
lessons.goal: İlgi cümleleri, betimleyici dil ve kişisel deneyimlerle zenginleştirilmiş, yayınlanabilir kalitede bir gezi yazısı yazabilirim.

discover.title: Örnek gezi yazısı: Kaçkarlar'da bir yayla
discover.body:
At 2,000 metres, the clouds sit below you.

That was my first thought as I stepped out of the minibus in Pokut, a tiny highland village in the Kaçkar Mountains, which I had dreamed of visiting for years.

The village, which is only open from June to September, consists of about thirty wooden houses, most of which belong to families from the valleys below. There are no shops and almost no phone signal, which, I quickly realised, was exactly the point.

Our host, Fadime Teyze, whose family has spent every summer here for four generations, welcomed us with fresh bread, butter and a cheese called minci. In the evening, we sat on her wooden balcony and watched the sun sink into a sea of clouds.

If you go, bring warm clothes, even in August. And leave your laptop at home. You won't need it.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest leaving at home?

learn.explanation:
**İyi bir gezi yazısının özellikleri:**

| Bölüm | İpucu | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **Çarpıcı giriş** | Bir görüntü, bir an ya da bir cümleyle başlayın. | *At 2,000 metres, the clouds sit below you.* |
| **Konum ve bağlam** | Yeri kısa ve somut tanıtın. | *Pokut, a tiny highland village in the Kaçkar Mountains, ...* |
| **Ayrıntılı betimleme** | Non-defining clauses ile ek bilgi ekleyin. | *The village, which is only open in summer, ...* |
| **İnsanlar ve kültür** | Yerel bir kişi, yemek ya da gelenek. | *Our host, whose family has ...* |
| **Kişisel yorum** | which ile duygu / yorum ekleyin. | *..., which was exactly the point.* |
| **Pratik tavsiye ve kapanış** | Kısa ve akılda kalıcı. | *Leave your laptop at home. You won't need it.* |

**Üslup ipuçları:**

- **Cümle uzunluğunu değiştirin**: uzun betimleyici cümlelerin arkasından kısa vurucu cümleler.
- **Apposition** (açıklayıcı isim grubu) kullanın: *Pokut, **a tiny highland village**, ...* (which is'siz kısa non-defining)
- **Şimdiki zaman** yerin genel özelliklerini, **geçmiş zaman** sizin deneyiminizi anlatır.
- Klişelerden kaçının: *hidden gem, paradise on earth* gibi ifadeleri az kullanın.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçe gezi yazılarında bilgi ve kişisel deneyim genellikle ayrı paragraflarda verilir. İngilizce gezi yazısında (travel writing) ikisi iç içedir: Yazar okuyucuyu kendi gözünden geziye çıkarır. Non-defining relative clauses ve apposition, bilgiyi cümlenin akışını bozmadan eklemenin en etkili yoludur.

Çarpıcı bir girişle başlayın; en az 4 non-defining relative clause, bir cümleye yorum ekleyen which, bir miktar + of which / whom ve bir apposition kullanın. task.modelAnswer:
The ferry horn sounds twice, and suddenly the noise of Istanbul disappears behind you.

Büyükada, the largest of the Princes' Islands, is only ninety minutes from the city centre, but it feels like another century. There are no private cars on the island, which means the only sounds are seagulls, bicycle bells and the quiet hum of electric buggies.

I spent a long weekend in a small guesthouse near the harbour. The owner, Rebeka Hanım, whose grandparents built the house in 1910, served breakfast in a garden full of roses and fig trees. She told me stories about the island's past, much of which I had never heard before.

The island is famous for its grand wooden mansions, many of which were built by wealthy families in the late nineteenth century. Some are beautifully restored; others are slowly falling apart, which gives the streets a strange, romantic sadness.

The best way to explore is on foot or by bicycle. Climb up to the Aya Yorgi Monastery, which sits on the island's highest hill, and you'll be rewarded with a breathtaking view of the Sea of Marmara.

A final tip: avoid summer weekends, when the ferries are packed. Go on a weekday in May or October, and you might feel as if you have the whole island to yourself.

questions.prompt: Türkiye'de turistlerin pek bilmediği bir yeri tanıtan bir gezi yazısı yazın (200–250 kelime). Non-defining relative clauses, cümleye yorum ekleyen which, miktar + of which / whom, apposition, konum fiilleri ve güçlü betimleme sıfatları kullanın. Kişisel bir deneyim ve pratik bir tavsiye ekleyin.
questions.modelAnswer:
Most people who visit the Black Sea go straight to Trabzon or Uzungöl. Very few take the narrow road east to Şavşat, a small town in the province of Artvin, which is a shame, because it's one of the most breathtaking corners of Turkey.

Şavşat lies in a lush valley surrounded by dense forests of pine and spruce. Just above the town is Karagöl, a dark mountain lake which reflects the trees so perfectly that it looks like a mirror. In autumn, when the leaves turn orange and red, the landscape is truly stunning.

I stayed in a wooden guesthouse run by a family, most of whom had never left the region. The grandmother, who was in her eighties, made fresh corn bread every morning and told me stories about the winters, some of which lasted six months.

The local cuisine is simple but delicious. Try the honey, much of which comes from tiny hives hidden in the forest, and the famous Şavşat cheese.

There's not much nightlife, and the phone signal is weak, which, after a busy year in Istanbul, was exactly what I needed.

If you go, rent a car, because public transport is limited. The best time to visit is late September or early October, when the forests are at their most colourful and the summer crowds have gone.
